title: GuitarLab Spiral Learning Framework

principles: Integrate sound, rhythm, technique, fretboard knowledge, theory and repertoire from the beginning.
Use focused repetition for unfamiliar movements; introduce mixed practice when the learner has a stable foundation.
Use spaced retrieval and adaptive review rather than punitive streaks.
Treat elapsed time as practice context, never as proof of mastery.
Keep learner choice, self-assessment and musical enjoyment visible.

spiralStrands.title: Sound, pulse and rhythm
examples: tap or count a steady pulse
clap or speak a rhythm before playing it
listen for starts, stops, rests and accents
use a metronome or backing track when useful

spiralStrands.title: Ear, singing and audiation
examples: hum or sing the target note or phrase
call-and-response with notes or rhythms
hear whether a phrase rises, falls or repeats
match a heard sound on the guitar
gradually identify intervals, roots and chord quality

spiralStrands.title: Technique, tone and comfort
examples: relaxed setup and minimal necessary pressure
clean fretting and picking
short focused repetitions
notice unnecessary tension and rest when needed

spiralStrands.title: Fretboard and applied theory
examples: name strings and selected note landmarks
connect fret movement to semitones
relate chord shapes to roots and intervals
map scales and triads progressively

spiralStrands.title: Repertoire and creativity
examples: apply a skill to a small musical phrase
use a progression or song section
create a variation or two-note motif
build repertoire across styles

spiralStrands.title: Reflection and retrieval
examples: recall without looking at the answer
record one success and one difficulty
choose one next target
review older skills after a delay

practicePlans.rule: Do not compress every activity into a short session. Select the highest-value task for the available time.

practiceProgression.newSkill: Start with focused repetition at a comfortable tempo, then combine the skill with a familiar task after it becomes reasonably stable.
practiceProgression.mixedPractice: Introduce interleaving progressively; do not force random switching for every task because music-practice findings vary by learner, instrument and task.
practiceProgression.tempo: Increase tempo only after the exercise-specific quality target is met. If accuracy, tone or comfort drops, reduce tempo.

signals: hesitation or response time where measurable
application in a new musical context
rules: Schedule earlier review after errors, hesitation or low confidence.
Extend the interval after confident retrieval on separate occasions.
Occasionally ask for recall before showing diagrams or answers.
Bring stable skills back in new musical contexts.
Treat review dates as suggestions, not deadlines.
reviewPolicy.note: Initial intervals are configurable product heuristics and must not be described as a scientifically optimal schedule.

assessment.defaultMasteryGuidance: Require more than one successful demonstration separated in time and at least one application beyond an isolated drill. Make the rule visible and allow learner review.
assessment.limitations: Only label a result measured when an implemented, validated tool measured that exact property.

checkpoints.performance: A short chord and melody medley with steady pulse
A chord piece, a melody and a short lead phrase
A selected chord, rhythm and melody task
Prepared piece, short sight-read or TAB excerpt and improvised phrase
Accurate note finding and triad recall; time is secondary
Scale fragment, musical phrase and chord-tone landing
Strummed and fingerpicked versions of a short section
Short melody, comping and solo arrangement
Prepared piece, progression and short improvised phrase

guidance: Use stable instrument support and a comfortable setup.
Use only the pressure needed for a clear note.
Take breaks and avoid long forced repetitions.
Stop the exercise if pain, numbness or tingling occurs; seek qualified professional advice for persistent symptoms.
physicalComfort.disclaimer: GuitarLab is an educational tool, not a medical or rehabilitation service.

contentAuthoring.existingOutlineCompatibility: The existing weekly records remain valid outlines; optional detailed fields are added progressively with versioned schemas.

progressionConstraints: Keep Year 1 and Year 2 week IDs stable.
Keep weekly curriculum progress separate from numbered micro-lesson progress.
Do not force a seven-day week or a five-day practice streak.
Do not gate progress on optional staff notation.
Choose Year 3+ specialisation by learner interest and demonstrated prerequisite skills, not calendar time alone.
